runs.text: When your satellite is predicted to pass close to another object, simulate candidate avoidance maneuvers and compare their safety and fuel use.
Choose a conjunction event that has triggered an alert.
Vary burn magnitude and time to create Actors (maneuver scenarios).
Compare scores for collision probability, new conjunctions, and fuel use.

runs.text: Click My STM at the top of the left sidebar.
My STM holds the satellites you manage. No satellites have been added in this example.
The initial view shows the full object list on the right: Object Filter, with 18,798 objects.

runs.text: The button is at the upper right of My Satellites (0). An empty list means no satellites have been added.
Nearby controls include Orbit, Tag, Cone, Remove, and the My Ground Sensors tab.

runs.text: Enter RAZAKSAT or 35578 to find the satellite.
Select RAZAKSAT in the results. It appears in Selected on the right. Click Submit (1) to add it to My STM.
Searching for 35578 also returns STARLINK-35578 (66168). Check the NORAD ID carefully.

runs.text: Confirm the satellite and open Conjunction Assessment
Check that RAZAKSAT 35578 appears in My Satellites (1).
The RAZAKSAT label and orbit also appear on the 3D globe.
Then click Service › Astro-1 › Conjunction Assessment.

runs.text: Review events in the Conjunction Table
Change the reference time to review conjunction events.
Use the time selector at the top, for example 2026-10-06 00:00, to view the Conjunction Table for that time.
My STM Conjunctions lists RAZAKSAT events in DCA order.
Example: row 1, OBJECT G. TCA Oct 07 17:24:33. DCA 1.780 km.

runs.text: Click the graph icon in the Info column of Object Filter.
Click Expand Panel at the upper right for a wider view.
Click ‹ List to return to the list.
The Info icon is available in both the My STM and Objects tables.

runs.text: < 03 · Run COLA · Example 1: IRIDIUM 33 DEB · 2/6 Manual >
Enter Manual maneuvers and run COLA
Add Actors to RAZAKSAT, then click Run COLA.
This example uses 4 Actors: ΔV 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, and 1 m/s. Burn time: Sep 15 03:33 UTC, except Actor 4 at 03:34.
Leave IRIDIUM 33 DEB without an Actor to calculate its Original orbit.

runs.text: < 03 · Run COLA · Example 1: IRIDIUM 33 DEB · 3/6 Manual results >
Click Success in the results list to open COLA Detail.
Example: 35578_34896 · Oct 07, 2026 00:07:41 · Success. MSG ID combines your satellite's NORAD ID and the other object's NORAD ID, separated by an underscore.
The trash icon on the right deletes the result. Avoid clicking it unintentionally.

runs.text: Advised to contact the satellite's administration
Earth station in Primorsky Krai, Russia
Public statements by France and Germany
Source: SRMC quarterly reports "Satellite Radio Monitoring Trends", 2014 Q3 – 2024 Q1; international: French/German MoD statements, CSIS, Ukraine SSA
Koreasat 5: an adjacent GEO satellite named as suspect
Intermittent interference, 1–2 MHz wide, within 10 dB
Monitoring of adjacent GEO satellites pointed to Chinasat 10 (110.5°E) as the suspected interferer
Asked China's radio regulator to confirm and act
Source: SRMC, "2014 Q3 Satellite Radio Monitoring Trends", p.69 (spectrum screenshots from the same page)
Koreasat 5: noise from an adjacent-orbit satellite
Signal interference from an adjacent-orbit satellite
If it persists, request cooperation from that satellite's administration
Frequency and offending satellite not disclosed
Source: SRMC, "2020 Q1 Satellite Radio Monitoring Trends" (Interference investigations, 3 cases)
Russia's Luch/Olymp parks next to Western GEO satellites
Luch/Olymp-K 1 stationed beside Intelsat 7, 901, 905 and others; closest ≈ 55 km (CSIS orbital data)
Approached French–Italian milsatcom Athena-Fidus at GEO; France called it "an act of espionage" (Parly, Sep 7, 2018)
Luch/Olymp-K 2 drifting east toward SYRACUSE 4A and GSAT satellites (Ukraine State Space Agency)
Two Intelsat satellites used by the Bundeswehr "are being tracked" by two Luch/Olymp (Pistorius, Sep 25, 2025)
Source: French MoD speech (Sep 7, 2018); CSIS Aerospace "Luch"; Ukraine SSA notice (Feb 24, 2025); German MoD speech (Sep 25, 2025)
Koreasat 5A hit by a mispointed Chinasat-10 earth station
Earth station using Chinasat-10 pointed inaccurately
Notified Chinasat and the Chinese administration; signal disappeared during investigation
Source: SRMC, "2023 Q4 Satellite Radio Monitoring Trends"; orbital positions from SRMC "2018 Q3" report
Same source, again: escalation to the Chinese administration
Koreasat 5 / 5A vs Chinasat 10 — a recurring pair
Koreasat 5 · Chinasat 10 named as suspect · request to administration
Transponder 8 · resolved by re-pointing the earth station
Earth station using Chinasat-10 pointed inaccurately
Notified Chinasat and requested action; notified the Chinese administration
Source: SRMC, "2014 Q3", "2023 Q4" and "2024 Q1 Satellite Radio Monitoring Trends"
ITU-BR asks Korea to locate a source hitting JCSAT-3A
Earth station in Primorsky Krai, Russia
SRMC sent its geolocation results to ITU-BR
Source: SRMC, "2022 Q2 Satellite Radio Monitoring Trends" (Interference investigations, 3 cases)
Korea SRMC "Satellite Radio Monitoring Trends" (quarterly) — 2014 Q3 (p.69, spectrum), 2020 Q1, 2022 Q2, 2023 Q4, 2024 Q1; 2018 Q3 for orbital positions ·
F. Parly, "Espace et défense", Toulouse, Sep 7, 2018 ·
B. Pistorius, BDI Space Congress speech, Sep 25, 2025 ·
State Space Agency of Ukraine, Luch/Olymp-K 2 orbital change, Feb 24, 2025 ·
Korean report titles translated. Facility names and some frequencies are withheld in the original SRMC reports.
